validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE NOT INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED. The gem.wiki row's ONLY outbound citation (wiki_citations.json) is a generic OPEC Annual Statistics Bulletin 2012, p.75 — a country-level statistics publication (production/reserves/exports) that does NOT name individual domestic pipelines, let alone a 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah 3' line. It cannot support existence of this specific pipe. Extensive web + Arabic searching (Aramco, Aramco Life, MEED, Saudipedia, GlobalData) returned NO independent source that names 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah' line 1, 2, or 3, or that distinguishes three parallel 43 km / 30 in Khuff-to-Hawiyah lines. Every search hit for the exact name traces back to gem.wiki itself. The genuinely independent, detailed MEED account of the Hawiyah pipeline programme names real lines by their Aramco abbreviations (HDUG-1 Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line, HUG-1 Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah gas line, plus NGL lines) — none of which is a 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah' line. GEOGRAPHY ALSO CONFLICTS WITH THE SPEC: Aramco program documentation states the Haradh and Hawiyah units are 'approximately 100 kilometres apart', yet GEM lists this as a 43 km line — a full Haradh-to-Hawiyah run cannot be 43 km, so the length is internally inconsistent with the named endpoints (spec concern). This row is part of a bulk P1897-P1925 cluster (all last-updated 2022-07-19) whose members carry engineering/GIS segment labels (e.g. 'UBTG-1-km56-AY-1 KP916', 'AY-1 KP 943', 'UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56'), strongly indicating an unverified import of GIS route segments rather than editorially confirmed pipelines. Skeptical verdict: flag for existence review; a human should recover the source dataset and decide whether lines 1/2/3 are genuine parallel pipes, segments of one system, or duplicates.

validity.recommendation: De-dup review of the Haradh-Khuff-Hawiyah triple (P1917 base / P1918 '2' / P1919 '3') — identical 43 km / 30 in / operating / same endpoints; confirm whether these are three real parallel pipes or a triple-count. Also cross-check against P3961 Madrakah-Al Hawiyah, which appears to capture the documented long-haul non-associated-gas line from the Haradh/Madrakah area to Hawiyah Gas Plant (290 MMscfd).
validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE/RELABEL RISK. P1919 is byte-for-byte identical in specs to its two siblings P1917 (Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah) and P1918 (Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah 2): all three are 43 km, 30 in, operating, ?->Al Hawiyah, Owner Saudi Aramco, updated 2022-07-19. No independent source distinguishes the three, and none confirms three separate physical lines exist. Aramco does run parallel transmission lines in this corridor (a search lead noted 'five 20-inch and 30-inch gas transmission lines totalling 130 km' feeding the Haradh plant), so parallel 1/2/3 is physically PLAUSIBLE — but plausibility is not verification, and the audit standard (>=2 independent naming sources) is not met for any of the three. Separately, the REAL, well-documented long-haul gas line from the Haradh/Madrakah ('Mudraka') area to Hawiyah Gas Plant (290 MMscfd of non-associated gas) is already carried in GEM as P3961 Madrakah-Al Hawiyah Gas Pipeline (450 km, cap 290) and corroborated by GlobalData (offshore-technology.com lists a 'Haradh-Hawiyah Gas' line at 450 km / 36 in, Aramco). The 43 km triple does not correspond to that documented line. GulfPub PE World Map (20 SA gas features) has NO counterpart for a 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah' line, further weakening independent support. Human de-dup pass needed.

fills.researcher_notes: Owner=Saudi Aramco is class-level attribution: all Saudi domestic gas transmission is owned/operated by Saudi Aramco, and GlobalData (offshore-technology.com) lists the Haradh-Hawiyah gas line owner/operator as Saudi Arabian Oil (Saudi Aramco). This is not line-specific verification of P1919 (whose distinct existence is in doubt), only of the operator class. Medium tier.

Fuel=Gas is consistent with the corridor: Saudipedia confirms Hawiyah Gas Plant processes non-associated sour gas from the Khuff (and Jauf) reservoirs of south Ghawar. Any Haradh-Khuff-to-Hawiyah line would carry Khuff gas. Class-level support, not line-specific proof.
No independent source corroborates 43 km for this line, and it conflicts with Aramco's statement that Haradh and Hawiyah units are ~100 km apart. Not fillable; length is itself a spec concern.

Endpoints are self-inconsistent: start is only 'Saudi Arabia' (blank), and EndState/Province='Makkah' is WRONG for Al Hawiyah / Hawiyah Gas Plant, which sits in the Eastern Province (Ash Sharqiyah), central-eastern Ghawar — not Makkah. (Note: 'Al Hawiyah' in Makkah is a different place near Taif; the Hawiyah Gas Plant is in the Eastern Province.) Not fillable without resolving the existence question first; the Makkah province tag is itself likely an attribution error.

routes.start_name: Haradh (Khuff gas area, southern Ghawar, Eastern Province)
routes.end_name: Hawiyah Gas Plant (central-eastern Ghawar, Eastern Province)
routes.corridor_desc: IF this line is real, the only defensible corridor runs NNE within the Ghawar field trend in the Eastern Province: from the Haradh area at the southern tip of Ghawar (~24.14N, 49.07E) up toward the Hawiyah Gas Plant in central-eastern Ghawar (~24.9N, 49.2E). This is a LOOSE bound: Haradh coordinate is the well-known town/field anchor; the Hawiyah Gas Plant coordinate is approximate (central-eastern Ghawar) and not precisely sourced. Aramco program docs put the Haradh and Hawiyah units ~100 km apart, which CONTRADICTS the sheet's 43 km length and the sheet's Makkah-province end tag (Hawiyah Gas Plant is in the Eastern Province). Corridor is unreliable until existence/length are resolved.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints inferred from named places: Haradh (well-known town, southern Ghawar) and Hawiyah Gas Plant (Saudipedia confirms it processes Khuff/Jauf sour gas from south Ghawar, Eastern Province). Coordinates are approximate/defensible-from-named-place, NOT surveyed; no route geometry was fabricated. The 43 km sheet length is inconsistent with the ~100 km real Haradh-Hawiyah separation, so suggested accuracy is LOW and the corridor should not be applied until the existence review resolves whether P1919 is a real distinct line.

summary: P1919 concern: existence unconfirmed (only cite is generic OPEC ASB 2012, no independent source names a 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah 3' line) + duplicate risk (identical triple P1917/P1918/P1919; real long-haul line is P3961 Madrakah-Al Hawiyah); length 43 km conflicts with ~100 km real Haradh-Hawiyah separation and end province 'Makkah' is wrong (Eastern Province).
